overview: The Fyfe Gambit answers 2...Nc6 with 3.d4, offering the d-pawn for open lines and development: 3...exd4 4.Nd5 or 4.Nf3 Bb4 5.Bd3. Black can keep the extra pawn, but must watch the e-file and f7. It is a rare surprise weapon that gives up central space for activity.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Nf3, Bd3 and castle
Use the open e-file and pressure on f7
Regain the pawn through tactics or a lead in development

black_ideas.idea: Take on d4 and keep the extra pawn
Trade pieces to neutralise the initiative

typical_structures.structure: Open centre, White a pawn down with open e- and d-files

character.notes: White sacrifices material for activity; the play is open and tactical.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the d-pawn but must defend accurately.

soundness.notes: Rare gambit, probably slightly worse for White but practical.

approach.notes: A fairly rare sideline, played for surprise.

character.reason: White gambits for open lines and quick development; tactical.

gambit.reason: White offers the d-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Playable gambit with compensation, not refuted.

structure.reason: Centre pawns come off straight away, open e-file.

approach.reason: Rare gambit that strong players seldom choose.

level.reason: Plans are clear but tactical accuracy matters.

plans.reason: White plays for development and f7 pressure.
